sessions.result: complete — NEW-1 (round 2's sole blocking finding) fixed at both layers: the live defect (CommentRow.tsx) and the enforcement gap that hid it (radius-token-only blind to a class string held in a variable). NB-2 and NB-3 (named 'also fix') fixed too.

evidence.NEW-1 defect (CommentRow.tsx:246-247): avatarClass ternary: rounded-full -> rounded-[var(--r-pill)] on both branches; non-agent branch's bg-[var(--surface-page)] -> bg-[var(--surface-elevated)] (same Set 3 second-job defect already fixed on Button/HostThreadSection/SearchField). Verified: npx eslint --config eslint.design.config.ts framework/design-system/src/CommentRow.tsx now reports 0 errors (was 2 before the fix, break-tested on the unmodified file first).
evidence.NEW-1 enforcement gap (chosen: option (a: tools/eslint-plugin-design/src/util.ts gained createConstIdentifierResolver (ESLint scope-manager based) plus an optional resolveIdentifier parameter on collectClassStringsFromExpressionDeep/collectClassStringsFromJSXAttributeDeep. Deliberately conservative: only follows a same-file identifier that resolves to exactly one const declaration with exactly one write reference (the initializer) — a let, a reassigned binding, an imported constant, or a runtime-computed value from props/state is NOT followed (stays invisible, a documented residual limit). Wired into both AZ7 rules that use the deep collector: design/radius-token-only and design/no-handrolled-control (the control-chrome axis shares the exact blind spot). scan.mjs and predicates.mjs (named in the finding as sharing the blind spot) got the same identifier-following via a per-file const map built with the TypeScript compiler API. CORRECTED (review round 3, R3-1): 'so their reported populations match the ESLint rule's' was not accurate — the scanners key their const map by name per file, not by lexical scope, which ESLint's scope manager is. Demonstrated both directions on one synthetic file: a module const plus a same-named function parameter makes a scanner report a violation that does not exist (false positive vs. the rule); the same name declared as a const in two different function scopes makes a scanner miss one the rule correctly flags (false negative vs. the rule). The scanners are an approximation of the rule's population, not an equivalent of it; the rule itself (ESLint, scope-aware) is correct. See the review-fix-3 session below for the regenerated migration-backlog.md and the new drift guard.
evidence.break-test: New RuleTester cases in radius-token-only.test.ts and no-handrolled-control.test.ts reproduce CommentRow's exact shape (ternary assigned to a const, then className={identifier}), a module-level extracted class-string constant, and a template-literal interpolation of an identifier — all now caught. A `let` that is reassigned after a token-legal initial value is a `valid` case, proving the resolver's conservative boundary (documented, not a false negative silently accepted).
evidence.repo sweep: git grep for the bare-identifier shape className={IDENTIFIER} across every layers/*/src and framework/*/src package found 47 sites carrying it besides CommentRow — almost all module-level extracted class-string constants (ArtifactStackItem.tsx's ROW/LEFT/TASK/TITLE/RIGHT/PILL, ErrorState.tsx's RETRY_BTN_CLASS(_COMPACT), ArtifactGalleryCard.tsx, ArtifactPreview.tsx, ArtifactEmbed.tsx, NavItem.tsx, Row.tsx, KnowledgeRow.tsx, Select.tsx, ItemList.tsx, SectionLabel.tsx, ReferenceChip.tsx, ArtifactKindBadge.tsx, PageHeader.tsx, Breadcrumb.tsx, RoleCombobox.tsx, ThreadRow.tsx, ArtifactTimestamp.tsx, plus 10 in a _dev-only demo page). Template-literal identifier interpolations (Avatar.tsx's colorClass, RoleCombobox's disabled-state ternary) are a related but textually different shape the regex doesn't match, also now covered by the resolver. Re-running npx eslint --config eslint.design.config.ts across framework/design-system/src and layers/core-ui/src (the full tree these two rules cover) with the fix in place reports zero design/radius-token-only and zero design/no-handrolled-control errors — CommentRow.tsx was the only production site actually carrying a violation of this shape; the rest were clean, just previously unverifiable.
evidence.NB-2 (Input textarea min-height): Input.tsx: split lg:min-h-[36px]/min-h-[44px] out of the shared INPUT_BASE into INPUT_SINGLE_LINE_HEIGHT, applied only to <input> mode. The textarea no longer carries any competing lg: height utility, so its own min-h-[80px] is the only min-height rule for it at every viewport (root cause was CSS-cascade order, not class-string order — lg:min-h-[36px] was winning at >=1024px regardless of where min-h-[80px] sat in the template literal).
evidence.NB-3 (surface-page still on two Input-se: Composer.tsx's reply textarea and RoleCombobox.tsx's trigger button + popover filter input: bg-[var(--surface-page)] -> bg-[var(--surface-elevated)] (RoleCombobox's trigger wasn't individually named in the finding but shares the file and the defect — fixed together for internal consistency, matching Input/Select/SearchField's own established fill).

evidence.mechanical drift guard (new): tools/repo-gates/src/design-backlog-drift.ts, wired into npm run verify via a new design:backlog:check step (same 'regenerate into a throwaway location and diff against the committed file' shape as the existing mock-inventory.ts --check). Reuses the real predicates.mjs + render-backlog.mjs unmodified — pointing render-backlog.mjs's ROOT argument at a scratch directory means check mode never mutates the real repo tree. Failure output names the actual drifted (axis, file, line-list) triples, not just 'something changed' (diffs by content, not by UI-### id, since ids renumber on every insertion — diffing by id would bury one real change in numbering noise). Hard-fails if predicates.mjs's own 'HARD FAIL: zero tsx' scan-empty guard fires (uncaught, propagates), and separately if the generator produces zero backlog items on an otherwise-matching run (a state migration-backlog.md's own scope line doesn't claim is reachable, so it reads as a scanner failure, not a success, and is treated as one). npm run design:backlog (write mode) regenerates the real file the same way a builder already does by hand per the file's own 'Regenerate:' line.

notes: Plan's radius finding is wrong: 3.35544e+07px is Tailwind v4 rounded-full (calc(infinity * 1px)), not an off-scale value. Real off-scale radii: 21. The genuine defect is the two spellings of pill.

Source measurement is worse than the plan's rendered-DOM measurement: 118 button recipes (not 47), 25 input recipes over a surviving DaisyUI control system, 79 uses of --surface-container in 27 shapes. Status is better: StatusChip forked in only 5 named places.

Root cause of non-enforcement: `npm run lint` runs `eslint . --quiet`, which does not run warn-level rules at all; every core-ui design rule is at warn; three plugin rules are registered nowhere; `npm run lint:design` crashes on main.
